summary: Sheng Yen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy, under Lingyuan and Dongchu, and earned doctorates at Rissho University. He held posts at Shandao Temple, Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and National Cheng Kung University.

Shenghai Li works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, and traditional teachers. He held fellowships at Harvard University and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Shenpen Hookham is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading and completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido, also studying under several traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

Shenphen Nangwa was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Önpo Tenzin Norbu, and others. He taught at Dzogchen Monastery in 1902 and served as the first khenpo at Dzongsar Monastery from 1918.

Sherab Chomphel specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the College for Higher Tibetan Studies, an M.A. from Banaras Hindu University, and studied for an MTS at Harvard University from 2022 to 2025.

Sherab Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Guru, Detsha, and Labrang monasteries, and Drepung Monastery. He served as president of the Buddhist Association of China (~1953–1966) and dean at the Buddhist Academy of China (1956).

Sherry B. Ortner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Bryn Mawr College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan. She held academic posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and UCLA.
Sherry Chayat is a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Vassar College from ~1961 to 1965 and trained under traditional teacher Eido Shimano from ~1967 to 1998.
Shesh Dev Pandey is an Indology scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University, earning a Shastri degree between 2020 and 2023.

Shi Hu was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Cornell University and earned a Ph.D. under John Dewey at Columbia University, later holding posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Academia Sinica.

Shi Wang works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Wang completed a B.A. at Yale University (2020–2024) and studied for a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2024–2025).

Shichang Ma was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He worked as a researcher in Buddhist archaeology at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held an archaeology department post at Peking University from 1982.
Shigeki Kaizuka was a scholar of sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1925 to 1928 and held an academic post there from ~1930 to 1968.

Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held an assistant post at Kyoto University and assistant professor positions at Shuchiin University and Shitennoji University, the latter attested in 1972–1973.

Shigeki Moro is a scholar of Buddhist studies, computational fields, and philosophy. He studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura, holding professorships at Hanazono University (2002–2025) and Waseda University (2025).
Shigemasa Fukui is a scholar of sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from ~1955 to 1959 and served as a professor there from ~1978 to 2006.

Shigemitsu Dando studied at the University of Tokyo under Seiichiro Ono (~1932–1935). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University (~1974–1977), and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1977–1983).
Shigenori Nagatomo is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held a post as a professor of religious studies at Temple University, attested in 1999 and 2017.

Shigeo Kamata was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Kodo Sawaki. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin University, ICPBS, and Matsugaoka Bunko.
Shigeo Yokoyama is a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from ~1974 to 1978. He held academic posts at Okayama University (~1983–1994) and Nara Women's University (~1994–2017).
